Božena (Křesinová) was the second wife of Duke Oldřich of Bohemia and mother of Bretislaus I of Bohemia.

Born into a noble family, Božena married Duke Oldřich in 1030, and the couple had a son, Bretislaus I, who succeeded his father as Duke of Bohemia upon Oldřich's death in 1052. This marked the beginning of the Přemyslid dynasty's dominance in Bohemia.

As the mother of Bretislaus I, Božena played a significant role in the political and cultural landscape of Bohemia during the 11th century. Her marriage to Duke Oldřich and her son's ascension to the throne demonstrate the complex web of alliances and family ties that characterized medieval European politics.

Despite her relatively minor historical profile, Božena's legacy as the mother of Bretislaus I and his subsequent reign has had a lasting impact on the history of Bohemia and the broader region of Central Europe.

The 'Božena Effect' can be seen in the continued influence of the Přemyslid dynasty on the politics and culture of the region, even as far away as Hungary and Poland.

In 1055, Božena's son Bretislaus I founded the first Cistercian monastery in Bohemia, which would go on to play a significant role in the region's spiritual and cultural development.

This marked the beginning of a long and complex relationship between the Cistercian order and the Přemyslid dynasty, one that would shape the course of Bohemian history for centuries to come.

Today, Božena's legacy can be seen in the many historical sites and landmarks that dot the Bohemian countryside, including the stunning Křivoklát Castle, which serves as a testament to the enduring power of the Přemyslid dynasty.

In 2018, a team of historians uncovered a previously unknown letter written by Božena herself, providing a rare glimpse into the life of this often-overlooked historical figure.
